ev.q: the predeparture testing requirement was associated with 52% lower postarrival SARS-CoV-2 positivity
The percentage of positive pools increased 56% from 17.9% (291 of 1,622)
were 52% less likely to be positive than were those when predeparture testing was voluntary
after adjusting for COVID-19 incidence in the flight’s country of origin, pool size, and collection airport
Effect of Predeparture Testing on Postarrival SARS-CoV-2–Positive Test Results
Postarrival RT-PCR testing results during March 20–June 11, when the predeparture test requirement was in effect, were compared with those during June 12–September 3

methods_quotes.q: To identify factors associated with positive postarrival SARS-CoV-2 pooled test results, bivariate comparisons and univariable logistic regression were performed.
Factors with significant univariable associations (p<0.05) were incorporated into a multivariable mixed effects logistic regression model that included collection airport as a random effect.
Sensitivity analyses were conducted by repeating the regression models using 4- and 8-week periods around June 12 and adjusting for the same covariates.
